title: An icon you drew comes out as an SVG file
goal: The reason somebody draws paths in this app is to get an icon out of it, and today there is no way to. Export offers PNG, JPEG and HEIC, which are all pictures of an icon rather than the icon. Give Export a fourth answer that writes a real SVG: the shapes you drew, as shapes, in a file any website, app or icon set can use.
notes:
Why this is p1 and not a later nicety: the user asked for the Pen on 2026-09-13 in these words, "I want the ability to draw more complex shapes than a rect - specifically polygons that can do both hard edges and bezier curves in a natural way. This will help us build ellaborate svg icons for example." The three Pen tasks give you a path you can draw and reshape, and then the SVG stops at the edge of the app. Drawing an icon you cannot get out is half the ask.

What exists today, checked rather than assumed:
- Sources/PhotonzRender/ImageCodec.swift:10, `ImageCodec.Format`, has exactly png, jpeg and heic. Every one is a bitmap.
- Sources/Photonz/ExportDialog.swift:43 is the three-way picker, with a 1x/2x scale row under it at :48 and a pixel size line at :54. Both of those need a different answer when the format is not a bitmap.
- `grep -ril svg Sources/` returns nothing. There is no SVG code anywhere in the app, so this is the first of it.

Where the writer belongs: PhotonzCore. It is pure geometry and string building, it must stay free of CoreImage and AppKit, and it is the layer that can be tested without a renderer. Only the fallback-to-a-picture case needs the renderer, so hand that in rather than importing it.

The design decision worth making deliberately: how coordinates are written. The document model is top-left origin and so is SVG, which is a rare piece of luck in this codebase, so the flip DocumentRenderer owns (docs/design/overview.md) must NOT be applied here. Getting that wrong produces a file that is upside down and looks like a rendering bug.

Depends on the path model, because a writer with nothing but rectangles to write is not worth reviewing, and on the Pen, because the try path above needs a drawn shape.

Design doc: extend docs/design/vector-paths.md with a section on what goes out, or start docs/design/svg-export.md and link the two. Say which elements each layer kind maps to, so the next person adding a layer kind knows they owe it an answer here.

Queue-driven app work targets the Next release, and per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it.

MERGED IN on 2026-09-13 from a duplicate the intake window filed before searching ('an-icon-you-drew-leaves-as-clean-svg', dropped). Two things it carried that were not here:
- Gradients. The app can put a gradient on a fill and on an outline, so the writer has to emit a gradient definition and reference it, and a document that uses one is the obvious thing to test with.
- Fonts. 'Text writes as the right kind of SVG element' is only half an answer: a <text> element renders in whatever the viewing machine has, so an icon handed to somebody without the font comes out wrong. Converting text to outlines is the safe answer and loses editability. Choose deliberately and say why.
Also scoped out explicitly, from the same duplicate: animated SVG (its own epic child, icon-animate) and importing SVG. This is export of a static drawing.
acceptance: Ships behind one new Next flag, Export what you drew as SVG, written up in the Experiments window like every other flag, and its description says it needs the flag the Pen ships behind
Export gains SVG beside PNG, JPEG and HEIC, and choosing it swaps the 1x and 2x row for something that means something for a vector file rather than showing a scale that does nothing
A path writes as a path: straight runs as straight runs, curves as curves, closed shapes closed, with the same fill, outline colour and outline width it has on the canvas
Rectangles, ellipses, lines and text write as the right kind of SVG element rather than all being turned into outlines, and a rounded rectangle keeps its rounding
A group writes as a group, with the order and the nesting the layers list shows

Anything the app cannot say in SVG, an image layer or an effect with no vector answer, is written as an embedded picture in the right place, and the export says plainly what it had to fall back on rather than silently producing something wrong
The file is clean: no empty groups, no transforms that do nothing, no generated ids nobody reads, indented so a person can open it in an editor and recognise their own drawing
The written file is checked by rendering it back and comparing it to the app's own render of the same document, not by reading the text
Tests in PhotonzCore for the writer, covering a path with a straight edge and a curve, a rounded rectangle, a group, a fill, an outline and the fallback case, written before the implementation
A gradient fill and a gradient outline survive the export, checked by rendering the file back rather than by reading it
Text is handled by a rule that still works on a machine without the font installed, and the audit says which rule was chosen and why
Try it: turn the flag on in Experiments, draw a shape with the Pen, press Command E, pick SVG, save, then open the file in a browser and see the same shape
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the exported file's text shown beside a picture of the canvas, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: merged a duplicate filed by the intake window; gained gradients and the font rule

Adversarial review before building. (1) The mock-free question is the Export dialog: a scale row means nothing for a vector file, so picking SVG must replace it rather than grey it out. Decision: show the canvas size in points plus, when there is one, an honest line saying how many layers will go out as embedded pictures, so you learn that BEFORE you save rather than by opening the file. (2) Shortest version that delivers the value: the whole point is 'I drew an icon with the Pen, I want the icon'. So paths, rectangles, ellipses, lines, text and groups go out as real elements with their real paints; everything the app cannot say in SVG goes out as an embedded picture in the right place and is named in the report. (3) Cut: arrows (a shaft, a head and a caption pill are three drawings, and nobody draws an icon with the arrow tool), highlights (multiply blend), angular gradients (SVG has no conic ramp) and any layer wearing effects or a blend mode. All four are picture fallbacks in v1, each named, each a follow-up. (4) Checked rather than assumed: this machine's CoreSVG (NSImage) renders clipPath, mask, userSpaceOnUse gradients, embedded base64 PNG and <title>, so the render-back check can actually verify the file rather than the text.

Plan: PhotonzCore/SVGExport.swift is the pure writer (geometry + string building, no CoreImage, no AppKit). It takes two closures so it stays pure: one that hands back a picture of a layer that has no vector answer, one that hands back a text layer's outline as path data. PhotonzRender/SVGExporter.swift supplies both (DocumentRenderer for the pictures, CoreText for the glyph outlines). The app gains the format, a Next flag and the dialog change. Verification is a render-back comparison in PhotonzRenderTests, not a string read.

Shipped. PhotonzCore/SVGExport.swift writes the file (pure: geometry and strings, two closures handed in for the picture of a layer with no vector answer and for the outline of a text layer's letters). PhotonzRender/SVGExporter.swift supplies both, and TextRasterizer.outlinePath turns words into glyph outlines through the same framesetter the canvas draws with. The app gains the flag next-export-svg (needs next-pen), SVG in the Export sheet, and EditorState.exportSVG.

Verified by rendering the file BACK, not by reading it: SVGExportRenderTests draws twelve documents twice, once through DocumentRenderer and once through the system's own SVG reader (NSImage reads SVG on this OS), and holds the two to one part in 255 averaged over the canvas. Covered: a path with a straight edge and a curve, a rounded box, an oval, a line, a bordered box, a group, an inside line, an outside line, an even-odd hole, a linear ramp, a radial ramp, outlined words, a shadowed shape falling back, and a photograph. 29 writer tests in PhotonzCoreTests. Full suite green: 6314 tests in 513 suites.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the probe. (1) The sheet's title said Export Image, which is wrong for a file with no pixels in it: now Export. (2) The first version said 'Background goes out as a picture: it is a picture rather than shapes', which is a tautology under a warning triangle. A photograph is not a failure, so the sheet now has two lines: 'Background rides along as a picture' with a photo icon, and the warning only for what genuinely could not be written, 'Path goes out as a picture: it wears a shadow'. (3) Export now opens on the format you picked last time, because exporting a set of icons should be picking SVG once. (4) Left rough, each filed: arrows/highlights/measurements ride out as pictures (an-exported-redline-is-shapes-not-a-picture-of-o), shadows and blurs cost a shape its vectors (a-shadow-survives-the-trip-out-to-svg), and a blank canvas's white background is a 17KB bitmap inside a small icon (an-icon-exported-as-svg-has-no-picture-in-it).

Walk: Scripts/playtest/svg-export-walk.json draws a shape with the Pen, draws a box, writes the SVG through the app's own export path (new probe-only writeSVG step), photographs the Export sheet on PNG and on SVG, then puts a shadow on the shape and photographs the sheet naming it. Screen Recording is granted, so the audit carries real captures. Ran the walks I touched (export, frames): 6 passed, 0 failed.
